calibration.same_backend: classic Vulkan vs classic Vulkan, separate launches (driver restarts): static 30/30 and demo 87/87 ticks byte-identical across 3 launches each (max delta 0). Classic needs no tolerance; it exists only for the levelmesh.
calibration.cross_backend: classic GL33 vs classic Vulkan (known-good, different rasterizer): static 0/30 identical, max delta 24, 62.5% of differing px at delta <= 2, every cluster above delta 8 is a single pixel; demo 0/87 identical, max delta 208, 1-px-wide column clusters up to 1004 px (texture column / edge sampling). This is an upper bound on legitimate rasterizer noise, far looser than a same-backend levelmesh pair should be; thresholds that pass it would hide real bugs.
calibration.choice: channel 2 = one-shade colour rounding; min_cluster 4 = isolated edge-sample specks (< 2x2). Larger differences must be classified under a delta class (DC1 z-fight / DC2 float-z, ...) in a reviewed allowlist entry. Re-calibrate (abtest.py calibrate) if the reference machine or driver changes.
